overview.state_of_industry: The automotive industry is undergoing significant transformation driven by intensifying competition, continued supply chain volatility, and rising costs. New market entrants are challenging incumbents with competitive cost structures and faster development cycles — Toyota plans to sell US-made vehicles in Japan, China's BYD has overtaken Tesla as the world's biggest EV seller, and Foxconn is making EVs for Japan's Mitsubishi Motors. Legacy OEMs are responding: Ford's CEO Jim Farley stated they are 'redeploying capital into higher-return growth opportunities — Ford Pro, trucks and vans, hybrids'; GM described how it has 'structurally transformed over the past decade to focus on profitable growth and durable cash flows, with a leaner cost structure'; BMW anchors its strategy on 'a systematic focus on customers, a more flexible approach, and consistent cost discipline.' Supply chain disruptions have not gone away — DRAM makers are prioritizing AI demand over automotive, Honda has extended China production halts, and Ford expects to take a $1B earnings hit from supply chain issues. Automakers are transforming operating models to build resilience. Across the industry, AI is emerging as the key enabler — from cutting evaluation times in R&D to dynamic pricing and supply chain optimization.

overview.state_of_industry: To be curated from raw extraction

The Consumer Packaged Goods industry is navigating a fundamental shift in how consumers buy, what they expect, and how much power retailers now hold. Omnichannel has exploded from two touchpoints a decade ago to seven today — retail, marketplaces, direct-to-consumer, social commerce, last mile, B2B, and metaverse — representing a $1.5T US opportunity where omnichannel buyers now account for 91% of total purchases. At the same time, industry growth has decelerated from 5% at the turn of the century to near zero, driven by slower population growth, private label expansion, and macroeconomic pressure on consumer spending. Retailers are gaining leverage, squeezing terms, and demanding greater supply chain efficiency and compliance. Rising material costs (up 35% since 2019), limited end-to-end supply chain visibility (69% of businesses lack it), and deduction leakage (>10% of gross revenue) are compressing margins that were already under strain. The combination of external pressure and operational complexity makes process intelligence a strategic necessity — not a cost optimization exercise.
industry_challenges: Omnichannel complexity — 7 consumer touchpoints requiring seamless, flexible experiences across retail, DTC, marketplaces, and social commerce while integrating sustainability commitments

Supply chain disruptions — rising material costs (35% since 2019), geopolitical volatility, limited E2E visibility (69% of businesses), and transportation inefficiencies degrading ETA accuracy and customer experience
Deduction leakage — >10% of gross revenue lost to retailer and carrier deductions processed across 24+ disconnected portals with >1 month average resolution time
Retailer squeeze — retailers gaining negotiating power, demanding greater supply chain compliance (OTIF penalties increasing), tightening terms, and pushing private label growth
Innovation speed — only 31% of CPG leaders confident in their ability to accelerate innovation and scale rapidly; manual, cross-functional launch processes missing retailer sell-in windows

Economic pressure — industry growth near zero; private label capturing value-conscious consumers; escalating and volatile commodity costs requiring aggressive cost management and working capital optimization

overview.state_of_industry: Life Sciences brings together pharmaceutical, biotech, and MedTech organizations with one shared mission: to improve and extend human life. These companies operate in one of the most complex and regulated environments in the world. Three macro pressures define the current landscape: (1) continued global supply chain disruptions — 35% of pharma supply chains cannot respond to disruptions within 5 days, and $35B in pharmaceutical products are lost or wasted annually due to supply chain inefficiencies; (2) rising drug development costs and clinical trial variability — bringing a new drug to market costs $1-2B and takes over a decade, with only 12% of drugs obtaining FDA/EMA approval and 60%+ of trials experiencing protocol amendments; (3) healthcare reform and macroeconomic pressure — the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act, aging population demographics, and rising costs are forcing companies to prioritize financial discipline and commercial impact. Simultaneously, AI investment is accelerating — 80% of R&D executives say data fragmentation is their number one blocker to AI success. Celonis is uniquely positioned to solve the foundational process visibility problem that makes all of this harder than it needs to be.

By surfacing root causes of delays, compliance risks, and CRO performance issues, Celonis enables R&D teams to act before problems compound — accelerating timelines, elevating compliance, and grounding AI initiatives in trusted process data.

overview.state_of_industry: In 2026, geopolitical tensions, rising costs, and the rise of AI are reshaping global manufacturing. Geopolitical tensions are causing manufacturing leaders to prioritize tax incentives and reassess export controls. Long-standing considerations like labor costs, talent availability, and energy costs have become more acute as companies reassess risk and resilience — with 39% of respondents seeing increases in supplier and material costs. To protect against global instability, manufacturing leaders are re-thinking how their entire value chain runs. Simultaneously, operational efficiency is a board-level priority, with manufacturers under pressure to reduce headcount vacancies and restructure quickly as volatility demands it. The rise of Agentic AI has made leaders and budgets more open to investing in technologies that change how their people work — 90% of manufacturers are utilizing AI, and 71% of organizations now regularly use GenAI in at least one business function.
industry_challenges: Geopolitical volatility and tariff uncertainty reshaping demand and cost structures (70% of respondents say tariff impact on US demand equals or exceeds global impact)
Supplier and material cost increases (39% of manufacturers report increases)
Labor shortages and rising skill requirements with persistent vacancy rates above 5% at 1 in 4 manufacturers
Siloed systems (ERP, MES, PLM, WMS) preventing a shared, objective view of how the enterprise runs
Pressure to restructure value chains while maintaining operational continuity
Competitive pressure from AI-native manufacturers who can respond faster to disruption
Operational efficiency mandates requiring measurable output from AI and automation investments
overview.celonis_value_proposition: Celonis builds a living digital twin of manufacturing operations — a real-time, system-agnostic model that captures how work actually flows across ERP, MES, PLM, WMS, and production systems. Because manufacturers have this digital twin, they can finally answer which orders are late and why, how exceptions are really handled across teams, where plans break downstream when something changes, and how to prevent these issues from recurring. This is the operational context that AI needs to work — and that no single system can provide alone.
key_messages: Manufacturing leaders are reassessing their entire value chain — Celonis gives them the objective view of how their operations actually run to make those decisions with confidence
The digital twin connects your systems to give AI the operational context it needs to actually work
From idea to shipment — visibility drives prioritization drives results
